accepted.s: The Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 primarily addresses which of the following?
o: Domestic violence against women in private households
Sexual harassment of women at the workplace
accepted.x: The POSH Act, 2013 addresses sexual harassment of women at the workplace.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the principal subject of the legislation.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s: The guidelines laid down in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) were primarily concerned with:
o: Sexual harassment of women at the workplace
accepted.x: In Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, the Supreme Court laid down guidelines concerning sexual harassment of women at the workplace.
accepted.tq: Use the case-name and subject association to distinguish closely related women-centric laws.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding sexual harassment under the POSH Act:
1. Unwelcome physical contact or advances may constitute sexual harassment.
2. A demand for sexual favours may constitute sexual harassment.
3. Showing pornography is excluded from the definition unless accompanied by physical contact.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because showing pornography is itself included among the forms of sexual harassment.
accepted.tq: Find the excluded-looking statement that reverses an express part of the definition.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s: Under the POSH Act, an Internal Committee is required in every workplace having:
accepted.x: An Internal Committee is required in every workplace with 10 or more employees.
accepted.tq: Recall the statutory threshold and distinguish it from the Local Committee threshold.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding the Internal Committee under the POSH Act?
o: External member — Representative of an NGO or association familiar with the issue
Composition — At least half of the members must be women
accepted.x: The Presiding Officer of the Internal Committee is a senior woman employee. The District Officer sets up the Local Committee.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrong authority by separating Internal Committee functions from Local Committee functions.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
 a. Internal Committee
 b. Local Committee
 c. Internal Committee Presiding Officer
 d. Local Committee establishing authority

List-II (Feature)
 i. District Officer
 ii. Senior woman employee
 iii. Workplace with fewer than 10 employees
 iv. Workplace with 10 or more employees

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: The Internal Committee applies to workplaces with 10 or more employees; the Local Committee applies to workplaces with fewer than 10 employees; its Presiding Officer is a senior woman employee, and it is set up by the District Officer.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair of the senior woman Presiding Officer and eliminate mismatched codes.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s: A complaint under the POSH Act is ordinarily required to be made within how many months from the date of the incident?
accepted.x: A complaint is ordinarily to be made within three months; this period may be extended by a further three months in appropriate circumstances.
accepted.tq: Recall the basic limitation period and distinguish it from the extension period.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the time limits under the POSH Act?
o: Complaint within 6 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 90 days
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 90 days and employer action within 60 days
Complaint within 90 days, inquiry within 3 months and employer action within 6 months
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 30 days
accepted.x: The complaint is ordinarily filed within three months, the inquiry is to be completed within 90 days, and the employer is to act within 60 days.
accepted.tq: Keep the three separate statutory periods distinct instead of swapping their order.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated duty of an employer under the POSH Act?
o: Displaying the policy relating to prevention of sexual harassment
Transferring every complainant to another workplace
accepted.x: Employer duties include constituting the Internal Committee, displaying the policy, conducting awareness programmes and acting on reports. Mandatory transfer of every complainant is not stated as a general duty.
accepted.tq: Find the option that imposes an absolute duty not included among the listed employer responsibilities.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s: The penalty for failure to comply with the employer duties under the POSH framework may extend up to:
accepted.x: The penalty for failure to comply with the specified duties may extend up to ₹50,000.
accepted.tq: Test the exact monetary ceiling rather than the general nature of the penalty.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s: SHe-Box 2.0, under Mission Shakti, is best described as:
o: A fund exclusively providing maternity benefits
An employment exchange for women in rural areas
A single-window online system for complaint and tracking of Internal and Local Committees
A criminal investigation portal for dowry deaths
accepted.x: SHe-Box 2.0 is a single-window online complaint and tracking system for Internal and Local Committees under Mission Shakti.
accepted.tq: Match the digital platform with its operational function rather than its broad women-welfare context.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s:
With reference to SHe-Box 2.0, consider the following statements:
1. It is associated with the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
2. It covers public, private, organised and unorganised sectors.
3. The SHINE app was launched by the Railways for its staff.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. SHe-Box 2.0 is associated with the Ministry of Women and Child Development under Mission Shakti, while Railways launched the SHINE app for its staff.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional ownership, coverage and the related-app distinction without confusing the two platforms.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s: According to the reported Andhra Pradesh implementation figures for 2025-26, which of the following is correct regarding POSH committees and cases?
o: 88 Local Committees, 86 Internal Committees and 10,437 cases resolved
26 Local Committees, 10,437 Internal Committees and all 88 cases pending
10 Local Committees, 26,437 Internal Committees and 88 of 86 cases resolved
26 Local Committees, 10,437 Internal Committees and 86 of 88 cases resolved
accepted.x: The reported figures were 26 Local Committees, 10,437 Internal Committees and 86 cases resolved out of 88.
accepted.tq: Read the three figures together and reject reversed counts and altered outcomes.
accepted.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

accepted.s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is primarily classified as a:
accepted.x: The Act is a civil law protecting women from domestic violence, although other criminal provisions may also apply to related conduct.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the civil character of the Act and criminal provisions dealing with particular offences.
accepted.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the forms of domestic violence covered under Section 3 of the Domestic Violence Act?
o: Physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse
accepted.x: Section 3 covers physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete statutory classification rather than selecting a partial list.
accepted.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the scope of the Domestic Violence Act:
1. It protects a woman irrespective of the nature of her relationship with the respondent.
2. It applies only when the relationship has been formally registered.
3. Protection Officers and registered Service Providers assist the aggrieved woman.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because protection is not restricted to formally registered relationships.
accepted.tq: Spot the formal-registration limitation, which improperly narrows the Act's relationship-based protection.
accepted.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

accepted.s: Protection Officers under the Domestic Violence Act are appointed by the:
accepted.x: Protection Officers are appointed by the State Government. Registered Service Providers also assist the aggrieved woman.
accepted.tq: Ask which level of government holds the appointing authority.
accepted.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

accepted.s:
Match the relief under the Domestic Violence Act with its section:

List-I (Relief)
 a. Protection order
 b. Residence order
 c. Monetary relief
 d. Compensation order

List-II (Section)
 i. Section 20
 ii. Section 22
 iii. Section 18
 iv. Section 19

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Protection orders are under Section 18, residence orders under Section 19, monetary relief under Section 20 and compensation orders under Section 22.
accepted.tq: Start with the familiar protection-order provision and verify the sequential relief sections.
accepted.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding reliefs under the Domestic Violence Act is correct?
o: Several forms of relief may be sought in one case and the matter is to be disposed of within 60 days.
Relief is limited to compensation and does not include residence rights.
Only one form of relief can be sought in a case.
Temporary custody cannot be granted under the Act.
accepted.x: Multiple reliefs may be sought in one case, including residence, protection, monetary relief, temporary custody and compensation; disposal is contemplated within 60 days.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute restrictions by applying the Act's cumulative-relief structure and time limit.
accepted.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, which of the following have been identified as Protection Officers for implementation of the Domestic Violence Act?
o: DWCDA Project Directors and Revenue Divisional Officers
Police Superintendents and Village Secretaries only
District Collectors and Municipal Commissioners only
Judicial Magistrates and Members of Parliament
accepted.x: In Andhra Pradesh, DWCDA Project Directors and Revenue Divisional Officers are identified as Protection Officers.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific state-level implementation authorities rather than generic administrative officers.
accepted.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the reported Andhra Pradesh implementation figures for 2024-25 under the Domestic Violence Act?
o: 55 NGOs as Service Providers, 47,734 petitions, 23,644 Domestic Incident Reports and 7,307 final orders
47,734 NGOs, 55 petitions, 7,307 reports and 23,644 final orders
55 NGOs as Protection Officers, 47,734 petitions, 23,644 final orders and 7,307 reports
23,644 NGOs, 7,307 petitions, 55 reports and 47,734 final orders
accepted.x: The reported figures were 55 NGOs as Service Providers, 47,734 petitions, 23,644 Domestic Incident Reports and 7,307 final orders.
accepted.tq: Keep the institutional count and three case figures in their correct categories.
accepted.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

accepted.s: According to the reported Andhra Pradesh figures for 2025-26, which statement is correct?
o: 2,207 cases were addressed and ₹51,581 crore was paid.
51,581 cases were addressed and ₹9 crore relief was paid to 2,207 victims.
9 crore cases were addressed and 51,581 victims received relief.
accepted.x: The reported figures were 51,581 cases addressed, ₹9 crore relief paid and 2,207 victims assisted through the relief payment.
accepted.tq: Match each number with its unit—cases, money or victims—before selecting the option.
accepted.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

accepted.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, voyeurism is dealt with under Section:
accepted.x: Voyeurism is dealt with under Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, corresponding to Section 354C of the IPC.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact BNS section and distinguish neighbouring sexual-offence provisions.
accepted.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

accepted.s: Stalking under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is associated with Section:
accepted.x: Stalking is covered by Section 78 of the BNS, corresponding to Section 354D of the IPC.
accepted.tq: Use the adjacent-section comparison to distinguish stalking from voyeurism and cruelty.
accepted.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

accepted.s: Dowry death under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is provided under Section 80. Its corresponding provision under the Indian Penal Code was:
accepted.x: BNS Section 80 deals with dowry death, corresponding to IPC Section 304B.
accepted.tq: Link the new BNS provision with its corresponding old IPC provision without swapping it with cruelty.
accepted.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

accepted.s: Cruelty by a husband or his relatives is covered under which provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
accepted.x: Cruelty by a husband or relatives is covered under BNS Sections 85-86, corresponding to IPC Section 498A.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the cruelty provision from the nearby dowry-death provision by section number.
accepted.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

accepted.s: For the purpose of the dowry-death provision, the relevant death is one occurring within how many years of marriage?
accepted.x: The dowry-death provision refers to a death occurring within seven years of marriage.
accepted.tq: Recall the statutory time threshold and avoid substituting common alternative periods.
accepted.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

accepted.s:
Match the offence with the corresponding BNS provision:

List-I (Offence)
 a. Rape
 b. Trafficking of persons
 c. Selling or buying minors for prostitution
 d. Acid attack

List-II (BNS provision)
 i. Sections 98-99
 ii. Sections 63-64
 iii. Section 124
 iv. Section 143

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Rape is covered by Sections 63-64, trafficking by Section 143, selling or buying minors for prostitution by Sections 98-99, and acid attack by Section 124.
accepted.tq: Begin with the sure rape pair and use elimination to place the remaining BNS provisions.
accepted.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding selected provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:
1. Sections 74 and 75 deal respectively with outraging the modesty of a woman and sexual harassment.
2. Section 67 concerns intercourse with a separated wife and prescribes imprisonment of two to seven years.
3. Section 124 concerns trafficking of persons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Section 124 concerns acid attack; trafficking of persons is covered under Section 143.
accepted.tq: Catch the swapped-offence trap between the acid-attack and trafficking provisions.
accepted.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

accepted.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, rape is dealt with under Sections 63-64, corresponding to which IPC provisions?
accepted.x: BNS Sections 63-64 correspond to IPC Sections 375-376. The stated exception excludes a wife aged 18 years or above from the rape provision.
accepted.tq: Match the new section pair with the correct old-code pair rather than a neighbouring offence pair.
accepted.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

accepted.s: Under BNSS Section 144, maintenance of wives is available:
o: Only to wives belonging to a specified religion
Only when domestic violence has been proved
Only when the marriage is less than seven years old
accepted.x: BNSS Section 144 provides for maintenance of wives regardless of religion; it corresponds to old CrPC Section 125.
accepted.tq: Reject the religion-based limitation and apply the express universal qualification.
accepted.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

accepted.s: The Supreme Court is examining the marital rape exception in relation to which of the following provisions?
o: The domestic-violence relief provisions under Sections 17-22
The rape provisions under BNS Sections 63-64
The maintenance provision under BNSS Section 144
The trafficking provision under BNS Section 143
accepted.x: The Supreme Court is examining the marital rape exception associated with the rape provisions under BNS Sections 63-64.
accepted.tq: Connect the constitutional-legal issue with the relevant offence provision rather than a related women-protection law.
accepted.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism
